EMPLOYEE LITERACY EDUCATION ASSISTANCE ACT — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jane Doe · Acme Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This document explains California's Employee Literacy Education Assistance Act, Labor Code §§ 1040-1044 -- a narrow statutory chapter addressing what happens when an employee reveals to their employer that they have a problem with illiteracy. It covers the chapter's coverage threshold, the accommodation-and-assistance duty it creates, what counts as "employer assistance," the employer's privacy-safeguarding duty, the chapter's own statement that it does not require paid time off, and its specific protection against termination based on the disclosure.

This chapter is a distinct statutory scheme from disability-accommodation law: it is not part of the Fair Employment and Housing Act or the Americans with Disabilities Act, and illiteracy is not treated here as a disability triggering those separate accommodation frameworks. This document does not address, and is not a substitute for, this corpus's separate ADA Reasonable Accommodation Request Form or Pregnant Workers Fairness Act Accommodation Request documents, which concern different statutory schemes entirely. This document also does not instruct any employee on whether or how to disclose a literacy problem, and does not instruct any employer on how to respond to a particular request -- it states only what the statute itself says.

Employee: Jane Doe
Employer: Acme Inc.

THE STATUTE'S NAME AND SCOPE
The chapter of the Labor Code addressed in this document is formally named the Employee Literacy Education Assistance Act. It consists of five sections, numbered 1040 through 1044, appearing within the Labor Code's general employment-regulation provisions on privileges and immunities.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Employee Literacy Education Assistance Act."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1040 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1040, short title (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1040.)
  Known gap: This naming section imposes no obligation on its own -- it only establishes the chapter's title and numbering. The threshold, duty, and protection provisions live in the sections that follow, and each of those carries its own separate limitation (a size threshold, an undue-hardship qualifier, and no stated penalty provision, among others), so the short title by itself does not indicate who is covered or what is required. No case law is cited for this section because a CourtListener case-law search for this chapter returned a 429 daily-rate-limit-exceeded error before any results could be reviewed, and this research session did not wait out or retry that quota.

THE ACCOMMODATION-AND-ASSISTANCE DUTY
A private employer that regularly employs 25 or more employees is required to reasonably accommodate and assist an employee who reveals a problem of illiteracy and requests the employer's assistance in enrolling in an adult literacy education program. This duty is qualified: it applies only if the requested accommodation does not impose an undue hardship on the employer.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Every private employer regularly employing 25 or more employees shall reasonably accommodate and assist any employee who reveals a problem of illiteracy and requests employer assistance in enrolling in an adult literacy education program, provided that this reasonable accommodation does not impose an undue hardship on the employer."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1041 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1041(a), accommodation-and-assistance duty and undue-hardship qualifier (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1041.)
  Known gap: The statute conditions the duty on the employer "regularly employing 25 or more employees," but its text does not define that phrase -- it states no measurement period, no method for counting part-time employees or employees across multiple locations, and no cross-reference to how the phrase is defined elsewhere in the Labor Code. The statute also does not define "undue hardship" or list any factors for weighing it, unlike some other California accommodation statutes that enumerate specific hardship factors, and it sets no deadline by which the employer must respond to a request. By its own terms the duty applies only to a "private employer"; the text does not say whether or how a public-sector employer is covered. No case law construing any of these terms is cited here because a CourtListener search for this statute returned a 429 daily-quota-exceeded error before results could be reviewed.

WHAT "EMPLOYER ASSISTANCE" MEANS
The statute describes employer assistance to include, without limitation, providing the employee with the locations of local literacy education programs, or arranging for a literacy education provider to visit the jobsite.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "For purposes of this section, employer assistance includes, but is not limited to, providing the employee with the locations of local literacy education programs or arranging for a literacy education provider to visit the jobsite."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1041 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1041(b), definition of employer assistance (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1041.)
  Known gap: The statute's list is expressly non-exhaustive ("includes, but is not limited to"), so its outer boundary is not fixed by the text itself. The two named examples describe directing an employee to existing resources or arranging an on-site provider visit; the statute does not say whether an employer must pay any cost of the literacy program itself, does not specify any minimum duration for which assistance must continue, and does not address what other forms of assistance, if any, a court might find required beyond these two examples. No case law is cited because CourtListener's search quota was exhausted for this research session before this statute could be queried.

DUTY TO SAFEGUARD PRIVACY
The statute requires the employer to make reasonable efforts to safeguard the privacy of the employee as to the fact that the employee has a problem with illiteracy.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The employer shall make reasonable efforts to safeguard the privacy of the employee as to the fact that he or she has a problem with illiteracy."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1042 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1042, privacy-safeguarding duty (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1042.)
  Known gap: The duty is to make "reasonable efforts," not to guarantee confidentiality, and the statute does not itself state what counts as a reasonable effort or list any exceptions -- for example, disclosure required by another law, or disclosure to a supervisor who has a legitimate need to know -- the way some other California confidentiality statutes expressly do. The statute also states no remedy specific to a violation of this privacy duty; any remedy would have to come from some other source of law not addressed in this document. No case law construing this duty is cited because a CourtListener search for this statute returned a 429 daily-quota-exceeded error before any results could be reviewed.

NO PAID TIME OFF REQUIRED BY THIS CHAPTER
The statute states that nothing in this chapter is to be construed to require an employer to provide time off with pay for an employee to enroll and participate in an adult literacy education program.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to require an employer to provide time off with pay for an employee to enroll and participate in an adult literacy education program."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1043 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1043, no paid-time-off requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1043.)
  Known gap: This section forecloses only one specific reading of the chapter -- that the chapter itself creates a right to paid time off. Its text does not say whether an employee may instead use their own accrued vacation, paid time off, or other paid leave for this purpose, and it does not address how this chapter interacts with any other, separately governed leave or accommodation entitlement an employee's particular circumstances might independently trigger. No case law is cited because CourtListener's daily search quota was already exhausted when this statute was researched.

PROTECTION AGAINST TERMINATION FOR DISCLOSURE
The statute provides that an employee who reveals a problem of illiteracy, and who satisfactorily performs their work, is not subject to termination of employment because of the disclosure of illiteracy.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An employee who reveals a problem of illiteracy and who satisfactorily performs his or her work shall not be subject to termination of employment because of the disclosure of illiteracy."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1044 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Lab. Code § 1044, protection against termination for disclosure (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1044.)
  Known gap: This protection, by its own text, reaches only "termination of employment." It does not use the broader language -- discharge, demotion, suspension, or other discrimination in the terms and conditions of employment -- that some other, similarly structured California leave and accommodation statutes in this corpus use, so its plain wording does not itself state whether it also reaches those other adverse actions. The protection is also expressly conditioned on the employee "satisfactorily" performing their work, a standard the statute does not define. Separately, this chapter's own text contains no penalty, treble-damages, or other explicit enforcement provision for a violation of this section, unlike some neighboring California leave statutes that state a specific remedy. No case law construing this section is cited because a CourtListener search for this statute returned a 429 daily-rate-limit error before any case-law results could be retrieved, and this research session did not wait out or retry that quota.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge review of this Employee Literacy Assistance information sheet.

Employee: Jane Doe
Employer: Acme Inc.
Date: January 1, 2026
